findings.description: A SIGHUP during a worker's slot wait used to end `pup session test` by node's default (129 to a shell). It is now caught and exits with the fixed 130. The gate maps the same signal to 128 + signum (129), and ADR 0096:38 still says only "Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during the wait ends it with exit 130". The fix is to use `128 + osConstants.signals[error.signal]` here, as `fatalExitCode` does, and to add SIGHUP to ADR 0096.

The per-signal closures built inside `WAIT_SIGNALS.map(...)` (registering listeners as a side effect of `.map` and returning `[signal, listener] as const` tuples) are more than needed: Node passes the signal name to the listener, so the old shared `onSignal` typed with `WaitSignal` plus `for (const s of WAIT_SIGNALS) process.on(s, onSignal)` / `process.off` in `finally` would do.

The new SIGHUP test copies the setup, listener-diff and assertions of the existing SIGTERM wait test (lines 244-257); an `it.each(['SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP'])` would cover both without the copy, and the title's "as on SIGINT" names a signal that has no wait test of its own.

The new sentence about the slot wait listening for SIGHUP is a bare paragraph between the `The rules:` list and `Owed`, so it reads as a detached note; it states a rule of the decision and belongs as a `- ` bullet in the rules list like the merge-lock SIGHUP bullet at lines 18-19.
The ADR's `Tests:` paragraph mentions only the merge lock's SIGHUP listener test, not the new `test-slot.test.ts` test for the slot wait ending on SIGHUP.
